title: ALMA observations of a z ≈ 3.1 protocluster: star formation from active galactic nuclei and Lyman-alpha blobs in an overdense environment
question: Is galaxy growth (star formation) of X-ray AGNs accelerated in the z~3.1 SSA 22 protocluster relative to field AGNs, and is star formation the power source of Lyman-alpha blobs?

what.value: Field X-ray AGN SFR comparison sample (ALMA 870 um)

evidence.quote: utilising the study of Mullaney et al. (2015), which primarily used ALMA 870 $\mu$m data to measure SFRs for $z>1.5$ X-ray AGNs in the field.

what.value: ALMA 1.1 mm data for protocluster core AGNs (incl. ADF 22a)

evidence.quote: Umehata et al. (2015) mapped this central region over 1.5$^{\prime}$ $\times$ 3.0$^{\prime}$ ($\approx$ 0.7 $\times$ 1.4 Mpc) with ALMA at 1.1 mm
The stellar masses of the protocluster AGNs have been calculated by Kubo et al. (2015)

what.value: Ly alpha luminosities / LAB definitions and narrow-band imaging

evidence.quote: All of our targets are detected in the narrow-band rest-frame Ly $\alpha$ imaging of Matsuda et al. (2004).

what.value: SFR evolution of M* star-forming galaxies

evidence.quote: we have assumed the measured SFR evolution for $M_{\rm *}$ star-forming galaxies from Schreiber et al. (2015)

recipe.method: Iterative CASA clean with natural weighting and tight clean boxes
key_parameters: clean to 1.5 sigma within boxes around >5 sigma then >3.5 sigma sources; 0.1 arcsec pixels

recipe.method: Find >3.5 sigma peaks in non-PB-corrected maps, repeat on inverted maps; adopt >4.5 sigma threshold; point-source fit for extension
key_parameters: 4.5 sigma threshold; upper limits = 4.5 x rms

recipe.goal: Match ALMA sources to X-ray AGNs
recipe.method: Combine Chandra (1.5 x 80% confidence) and ALMA (0.4 arcsec) positional uncertainties
870 um flux to L_IR(8–1000 um) with Bethermin et al. (2015) average SEDs, then SFR = L_IR/3.778e43 erg/s
assumptions: Chabrier IMF; L_IR uncertainty ~0.3 dex; z=3.09

recipe.goal: Compare protocluster and field AGN mean SFRs
recipe.method: Mean SFR ranges bracketing upper limits as 0 and as the limit; field AGNs evolved to z=3.09 using Schreiber et al. (2015)
assumptions: Field AGN SFR evolution follows M* star-forming galaxies

recipe.goal: Assess star formation as Lya power source in LABs
recipe.method: Convert IR star-formation luminosity to 200–912 A luminosity with Geach et al. (2009) template; derive required escape fraction

evidence.loc: 2.3 ALMA Source Detection, Matching, and Properties
evidence.quote: Overall we detect six ALMA sources at $>$ 4.5 $\sigma$ within the primary beam of the ALMA maps
the SFRs of the three ALMA-detected X-ray AGNs are $\approx$ 220–410 $M_{\odot}$ yr$^{-1}$

answer_key.quantity: SFR upper limits of undetected AGNs

evidence.quote: the SFR upper limits range from $<130$ $M_{\odot}$ yr$^{-1}$ to $<210$ $M_{\odot}$ yr$^{-1}$

answer_key.quantity: Mean SFR range of protocluster AGNs

evidence.quote: the mean SFRs of the protocluster AGNs are enhanced by a factor of $\approx$ 0.7–2.3 over the mean SFRs of the field AGNs

answer_key.quantity: Mean SFR of 6 core AGNs (with Umehata+15)

evidence.quote: is 500–530 $M_{\odot}$ yr$^{-1}$, a factor of $\approx$ 3.1–5.9 enhancement in mean SFR over that measured in the field
the mean and standard deviation is $240\pm110$ $M_{\odot}$ yr$^{-1}$

not_stated_but_needed: Exact clean parameters (niter, thresholds in Jy, mask definitions) and any uv-range selection
Flagging details and whether archive-delivered calibration was used or re-calibrated
Exact Bethermin et al. (2015) SED template and k-correction used to get L_IR from S_870
Individual field AGN SFRs from Mullaney et al. (2015) and Umehata et al. (2015) AGN values used for means
Method for the primary-beam-corrected upper limits for each non-detection
missing_for_reproduction: Exact SED templates and k-correction for L_IR
Field AGN SFR table values from Mullaney et al. (2015)
score_reason: Public Cycle 0 data, simple continuum imaging and clear numeric results; some inherited steps (SED conversion, field comparison) require external papers.
rediscovery_reason: Data are public, recipe is simple (clean, detect, flux to SFR) and results are numeric.
